concepts.name: Can explain Ricart-Agrawala Algorithm
concepts.description: The Ricart-Agrawala Algorithm is a distributed mutual exclusion algorithm that uses Lamport timestamps to order requests for critical section access.
check_questions: What is the role of Lamport timestamps?
How does the algorithm ensure safety?

concepts.name: Can analyze bandwidth usage of Ricart-Agrawala
concepts.description: The Ricart-Agrawala Algorithm has a bandwidth usage of 2*(N-1) messages per enter operation, which can be high for large N.
check_questions: What is the bandwidth usage for an exit operation?
How does this compare to other algorithms?

concepts.name: Can explain Maekawa's Algorithm
concepts.description: Maekawa's Algorithm reduces the number of replies needed for mutual exclusion by using voting sets, allowing only a subset of processes to grant permission.
check_questions: How does Maekawa's Algorithm differ from Ricart-Agrawala?

concepts.name: Can identify safety in Maekawa's Algorithm
concepts.description: Safety in Maekawa's Algorithm is ensured because a process can only receive replies from its voting set, preventing multiple processes from entering the critical section simultaneously.
check_questions: How does the intersection of voting sets contribute to safety?
What happens if two processes request access simultaneously?

concepts.name: Can analyze performance of Maekawa's Algorithm
concepts.description: Maekawa's Algorithm has improved bandwidth usage compared to Ricart-Agrawala, with O(√N) messages per enter operation, making it more efficient for large systems.
check_questions: What is the client delay in Maekawa's Algorithm?
How does the performance scale with N?

concepts.name: Can explain leader election in distributed systems
concepts.description: Leader election is a process in distributed systems to select a single process as the coordinator or leader among a group of processes.
check_questions: What is the purpose of leader election?
What happens if the leader fails?

concepts.name: Can describe the Ring Election Algorithm
concepts.description: The Ring Election Algorithm organizes processes in a logical ring and uses message passing to elect a leader based on attributes.
check_questions: How are messages passed in the Ring Election Algorithm?
What happens when multiple processes call for an election?

concepts.name: Can identify safety and liveness in election algorithms
concepts.description: Election algorithms must ensure safety by electing one leader and liveness by guaranteeing that the election process terminates successfully.
check_questions: What does safety guarantee in an election?
What is meant by liveness in this context?
